options: The oldest active transaction in the current database, including its start time and owning session
Every transaction ever run against the database, including committed ones
The total number of transactions per second on the instance
A list of all stored procedures currently executing
questions.explain: DBCC OPENTRAN is a fast, single-database check that surfaces only the oldest open transaction, if one exists.

questions.q: Which DMV maps a transaction_id back to the session_id that opened it?
questions.explain: sys.dm_tran_session_transactions is the bridge table between a transaction and the session that owns it.

questions.q: Why can a single open transaction cause the transaction log to keep growing?
options: In the full or bulk-logged recovery models, an open transaction prevents the log from truncating until it commits or rolls back
Open transactions automatically trigger a full backup
SQL Server doubles the log file size whenever a transaction starts
It only affects tempdb, never the transaction log
questions.explain: The log can't truncate past the log sequence number of the oldest open transaction, so the log keeps growing until it closes.

questions.q: What does an open transaction pin in tempdb under snapshot isolation or READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT?
options: The version store, preventing old row versions from being cleaned up
questions.explain: Row versioning keeps old versions around as long as any transaction might still need to read them, growing tempdb's version store.

questions.q: Which DMV lists every active transaction on the instance, server-wide?
questions.explain: sys.dm_tran_active_transactions is the server-wide list of every transaction currently active on the instance.
